keypoints_to_image2d — REPRCONV keypoint op

• Data kinds: keypoints → image2d

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.keypoints_to_image2d(keypoints, shape=(64, 64)) (to call the implementation directly, import reprconv; reprconv.keypoints_to_image2d(keypoints, shape=(64, 64)); from the registry, opsreprconv.get("keypoints_to_image2d"))

Usage

Image coordinates (N,2) = (u, v) → a count image (H, W). The second exit from keypoints.

Adds 1 at row round(v), column round(u). The quantisation onto the pixel grid is the loss: round-tripping with keypoints_from_image2d shifts positions by up to 0.5 pixel (measured on 225 well-separated points: per axis RMS 0.2835 px = matches the theoretical value of uniform quantisation 1/sqrt(12) = 0.2887. As a 2-D distance it is sqrt(2) times that, 0.4009 px, theory sqrt(2/12) = 0.4082). ★ This too was once gotten wrong: the measured 2-D distance was put next to the 1-D theoretical value and almost read as "should be 0.29 but it is 0.40" -- mixing per-axis quantities with distance quantities makes a correct implementation look wrong. Nearby points fuse as connected components, so the round trip can also reduce the number of points (measured: 60 points placed at random become 54 points).

Out-of-range points are not silently dropped -- dropping them would make it impossible to tell whether "detections decreased" or "the image was too small".

Args:

keypoints: (N, 2) (u, v).

shape: (H, W).

Returns:

(H, W) float64 count image.

Raises:

ValueError: invalid shape / non-finite / there are out-of-range points / shape exceeds the limit.
